name: Apollo 1 pad fire
lesson: Pure oxygen at 16.7 psia, above sea-level pressure, let ordinary cabin materials burn within seconds. Apollo switched to a mixed-gas atmosphere on the pad.

name: Mir oxygen-generator fire
lesson: A solid-fuel oxygen canister burned with its own oxidizer, so cutting airflow could not starve it. Dense smoke was the lasting hazard for the crew.

name: Apollo 13 oxygen tank
lesson: Not a cabin-atmosphere fire: damaged Teflon wire insulation ignited inside a service-module oxygen tank. Listed because it is the best-known oxygen fire in flight.

name: Artemis II smoke alarm
lesson: By crew accounts a cabin smoke detector tripped late in the flight. Details still to be checked against a NASA report; it shows that detection is a live question on Orion.
